newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan ship prepares for direct sailing to China.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan ship prepares for direct sailing to China.

text.p: The first ship to sail directly to communist China from Taiwan in 48 years will depart on Thursday from the island's southern Kaohsiung Harbour, shipping company officials said.

The Panama-registered Uni Order, owned by Taiwan's Uniglory Marine Corp, would sail directly across the Taiwan Strait and arrive in China's Xiamen port on Friday after a 12-hour voyage, Uniglory vice-president Wang Jung-hsiung said on Monday.

The sailing will come just days after the China-owned, Saint Vincent-registered Sheng Da travelled from Xiamen to Kaohsiung last weekend in the first direct voyage across the Taiwan Strait since 1949.
Wang said Uni Order was scheduled to depart Kaohsiung at around 0800 GMT on Thursday.
No ceremony was planned at either Kaohsiung or Xiamen to mark the occasion, Wang said.
For Taiwan shippers the voyage would be the first authorised crossing of the strait since 1949 when the Nationalists fled the mainland to the island after losing a civil war to the Communists.
Beijing's government regards the Nationalist-held Taiwan as a renegade province and vows to bring it under China's eventual rule, by force if necessary.
Taiwan, which has banned direct links with China since 1949, has agreed to allow limited direct shipping with the mainland under its "offshore transshipment centre" scheme.
Under the scheme, mainland cargoes are not be allowed to enter Taiwan customs but can be transshipped at Kaohsiung for onward passage to third countries.
Likewise, Taiwan cargoes at Kaohsiung cannot be put aboard ships planning to cross directly to the Chinese mainland.

Uniglory was approved by Beijing on April 17 to launch cross-strait shipping. China also gave permission to Taiwan's Yangming Marine Transport Corp, Wan Hai Lines, Nantai Line, Chinese Maritime Transport Ltd and Kien Hung Shipping.
The other five companies said they had no immediate plans to send ships to China.
